answer: Make identity expensive by tying it to a bond that only grows through checked work. An agent stakes a deposit, then earns standing slowly by finishing tasks peers can verify. From a knoll a newcomer sees the whole market, yet reaching the summit of trusted, high-value jobs takes a history no sybil swarm can fake cheaply, since each false identity needs its own stake and record. The sable line is cost: forging a thousand faces multiplies the price, while a caught cheat forfeits its bond.
